--- title: "Hands-on Exercise 4C" author: "ZHANG Xiaoyu" date: "May 07, 2026" date-modified: "May 08,2026" format: html code-link: true execute: eval: true echo: true warning: false freeze: true --- # Visualising Uncertainty Visualising uncertainty is a newer area in statistical graphics.In this chapter, you will learn how to create statistical plots for uncertainty. By the end of the chapter, you will be able to: - create error bar plots with **ggplot2**, - create interactive error bar plots with **ggplot2**, **plotly**, and **DT**, - create advanced plots with **ggdist** - create hypothetical outcome plots (HOPs) with **ungeviz**. ## **1. Installing and loading the packages** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pacman::p_load(plotly, crosstalk, DT, ggdist, ggridges, colorspace, gganimate, tidyverse) ``` ::: ## **2. Data import** This chapter we still use *Exam_data.csv*. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam <- read_csv("data/Exam_data.csv") ``` ::: ## **3. Visualizing the uncertainty of point estimates: ggplot2 methods** A point estimate is a single number, such as a mean. Uncertainty, on the other hand, is expressed as standard error, confidence interval, or credible interval. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam$MATHS <- as.numeric(exam$MATHS) my_sum <- exam %>% group_by(RACE) %>% summarise( n=n(), mean=mean(MATHS), sd=sd(MATHS) ) %>% mutate(se=sd/sqrt(n-1)) ``` ::: Next, the code chunk below will be used to display *my_sum* tibble data frame in an html table format. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} knitr::kable(head(my_sum), format = 'html') ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
RACE n mean sd se
Chinese 194 NA NA NA
Indian 12 60.66667 23.35237 7.041005
Malay 109 56.91743 21.74436 2.092352
Others 9 69.66667 10.72381 3.791438
````` ::: ::: ## **4. Plotting standard error bars of point estimates** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(my_sum) + geom_errorbar( aes(x=RACE, ymin=mean-se, ymax=mean+se), width=0.2, colour="black", alpha=0.9, linewidth=0.5) + geom_point(aes (x=RACE, y=mean), stat="identity", color="red", size = 1.5, alpha=1) + ggtitle("Standard error of mean maths score by rac") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex04C_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## **5. Plotting confidence interval of point estimates** Instead of plotting the standard error bar of point estimates, we can also plot the confidence intervals of mean maths score by race. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(my_sum) + geom_errorbar( aes(x=reorder(RACE, -mean), ymin=mean-1.96*se, ymax=mean+1.96*se), width=0.2, colour="black", alpha=0.9, linewidth=0.5) + geom_point(aes (x=RACE, y=mean), stat="identity", color="red", size = 1.5, alpha=1) + labs(x = "Maths score", title = "95% confidence interval of mean maths score by race") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex04C_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## **6. Visualizing the uncertainty of point estimates with interactive error bars** In this section, you will learn how to plot interactive error bars for the 99% confidence interval of mean maths score by race as shown in the figure below. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shared_df = SharedData$new(my_sum) bscols(widths = c(4,8), ggplotly((ggplot(shared_df) + geom_errorbar(aes( x=reorder(RACE, -mean), ymin=mean-2.58*se, ymax=mean+2.58*se), width=0.2, colour="black", alpha=0.9, size=0.5) + geom_point(aes( x=RACE, y=mean, text = paste("Race:", `RACE`, "
N:", `n`, "
Avg. Scores:", round(mean, digits = 2), "
95% CI:[", round((mean-2.58*se), digits = 2), ",", round((mean+2.58*se), digits = 2),"]")), stat="identity", color="red", size = 1.5, alpha=1) + xlab("Race") + ylab("Average Scores") + theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text( angle = 45, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1)) + ggtitle("99% Confidence interval of average /
maths scores by race")), tooltip = "text"), DT::datatable(shared_df, rownames = FALSE, class="compact", width="100%", options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX=T), colnames = c("No. of pupils", "Avg Scores", "Std Dev", "Std Error")) %>% formatRound(columns=c('mean', 'sd', 'se'), digits=2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## **7. Visualising Uncertainty: ggdist package** In the code chunk below, [`stat_pointinterval()`](https://mjskay.github.io/ggdist/reference/stat_pointinterval.html) of **ggdist** is used to build a visual for displaying distribution of maths scores by race. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam %>% ggplot(aes(x = RACE, y = MATHS)) + stat_pointinterval() + labs( title = "Visualising confidence intervals of mean math score", subtitle = "Mean Point + Multiple-interval plot") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex04C_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam %>% ggplot(aes(x = RACE, y = MATHS)) + stat_pointinterval(.width = 0.95, .point = median, .interval = qi) + labs( title = "Visualising confidence intervals of median math score", subtitle = "Median Point + Multiple-interval plot") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex04C_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## **8. Visualizing the uncertainty of point estimates: ggdist methods** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam %>% ggplot(aes(x = RACE, y = MATHS)) + stat_pointinterval( show.legend = FALSE) + labs( title = "Visualising confidence intervals of mean math score", subtitle = "Mean Point + Multiple-interval plot") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex04C_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## **9. Visualizing the uncertainty of point estimates: ggdist methods** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam %>% ggplot(aes(x = RACE, y = MATHS)) + stat_gradientinterval( fill = "skyblue", show.legend = TRUE ) + labs( title = "Visualising confidence intervals of mean math score", subtitle = "Gradient + interval plot") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex04C_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## **10. Visualising Uncertainty with Hypothetical Outcome Plots (HOPs)** ### **Installing ungeviz package** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} devtools::install_github("wilkelab/ungeviz") ``` ::: ### **Launch the application in R1** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ungeviz) ``` ::: ### **Visualising Uncertainty with Hypothetical Outcome Plots (HOPs)** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = exam, (aes(x = factor(RACE), y = MATHS))) + geom_point(position = position_jitter( height = 0.3, width = 0.05), size = 0.4, color = "#0072B2", alpha = 1/2) + geom_hpline(data = sampler(25, group = RACE), height = 0.6, color = "#D55E00") + theme_bw() + transition_states(.draw, 1, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](Hands-on_Ex04C_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.gif) ::: :::
